scenes.title: The Risk Management Mandate
scenes.purpose: The Risk Management Mandate: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: The Risk Management Mandate: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Global investment banks hold hundreds of thousands of complex derivative contracts across equities, commodities, interest rates, and foreign exchange.

hi.display: Sharma ji, kisi global investment bank ke paas hazaron stocks, bonds, currencies aur complex options hote hain. Bank ke CEO ko sham ko kaise pata chalta hai ki bank kitna paisa lose kar sakta hai?

en.display: In 1989, J.P. Morgan demanded a daily four-fifteen PM report summarizing firmwide market exposure in a single dollar number, leading to Value at Risk.

hi.display: Raju, 1989 mein J.P. Morgan ke CEO ne ek single page 4:15 PM report maangi thi jo poore bank ke market risk ko ek single dollar number mein summarize kare. Isse Value at Risk invent hua!

en.display: Yet the 2008 crash proved VaR is tail-blind. In Chapter 22 Part 1, we master VaR mechanics, Artzner's coherence axioms, and Expected Shortfall.

hi.display: Lekin 2008 crash ne prove kiya ki standard VaR tail losses par blind hota hai. Aaj Chapter 22 Part 1 mein hum VaR ki mathematics, Artzner ke Coherence Axioms, aur Expected Shortfall ko decode karenge!

scenes.title: Value at Risk (VaR) Mechanics
scenes.purpose: Value at Risk (VaR) Mechanics: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Value at Risk (VaR) Mechanics: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: The formal definition of Value at Risk states: we are X percent confident that portfolio loss will not exceed V dollars over an N-day horizon.

hi.display: Sabse pehle formal definition samajhiye: Value at Risk ek statistical statement hai: Hum X percent certain hain ki agle N dinon mein hamara portfolio loss V dollars se zyada nahi hoga.

en.display: Mathematically, VaR represents a specific quantile cutoff of the portfolio's cumulative projected loss probability distribution.

hi.display: Mathematical terms mein, VaR portfolio ke loss probability distribution ka ek specific quantile cutoff hota hai.

en.display: Historically, the Basel Committee established 10-day 99% VaR as the premier international benchmark for determining market risk regulatory capital.

hi.display: Global banking regulations mein Basel Committee ne historically 10-day time horizon aur 99 percent confidence level ko bank capital ka benchmark banaya tha.

scenes.title: Time Horizon Scaling: Square-Root-of-Time
scenes.purpose: Time Horizon Scaling: Square-Root-of-Time: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Time Horizon Scaling: Square-Root-of-Time: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: To convert a 1-day VaR to an N-day horizon, quantitative desks commonly apply the Square-Root-of-Time rule: VaR(N) = VaR(1) times square root of N.

hi.display: Agar aapke paas 1-day VaR calculated hai, toh N-day VaR nikalne ke liye square-root-of-time rule use kiya jaata hai: VaR of N days equals 1-day VaR multiplied by square root of N.

en.display: A crucial theoretical warning: this scaling strictly requires daily returns to be independently and identically distributed normal variables with zero mean.

hi.display: Lekin warning: ye rule strictly tabhi valid hai jab daily market returns independent, identically distributed, aur normal distribution follow karte hon jahan drift zero ho.

en.display: During real-world market crashes featuring volatility clustering and illiquidity, the square root rule severely understates multi-day tail risk!

hi.display: Real market crash ke dauran jab volatility cluster hoti hai aur market illiquid ho jata hai, toh square root of time rule actual cumulative losses ko grossly underestimate karta hai!

scenes.title: Artzner's Coherence Axioms
scenes.purpose: Artzner's Coherence Axioms: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Artzner's Coherence Axioms: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: In 1999, Philippe Artzner and his colleagues formulated four non-negotiable mathematical axioms defining what constitutes a Coherent Risk Measure.

hi.display: 1999 mein Philippe Artzner aur unke mathematicians ne risk measures ke liye 4 non-negotiable scientific axioms formulate kiye, jinhe Coherent Risk Measures kaha jata hai.

en.display: The first three are Monotonicity: larger losses mean greater risk; Translation Invariance: adding cash reduces risk; and Positive Homogeneity: scaling positions scales risk.

hi.display: Pehla hai Monotonicity: zyada loss ka matlab zyada risk. Dusra hai Translation Invariance: cash add karne se capital utna hi badhta hai. Teesra hai Positive Homogeneity: position double karne se risk double hota hai.

en.display: The fourth and most critical axiom is Subadditivity: merging portfolios must never produce more total risk than the sum of their individual risks.

hi.display: Aur chautha sabse critical axiom hai Subadditivity: kisi bhi do portfolios ko merge karne par total risk unke individual risks ke sum se kam ya barabar hona chahiye. Diversification se risk kabhi badhna nahi chahiye!

scenes.title: VaR Subadditivity Failure
scenes.purpose: VaR Subadditivity Failure: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: VaR Subadditivity Failure: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Now examine the greatest conceptual flaw of modern risk management: Value at Risk mathematically violates the Subadditivity axiom!

hi.display: Ab aate hain derivative finance ke sabse bade shock par: Value at Risk Subadditivity axiom ko mathematically violate karta hai!

en.display: Consider two independent corporate loans, each with a 0.8% default probability and $1,000 loss. At a 99% confidence level, VaR for each is zero dollars.

hi.display: Example dekhiye: Maan lijiye Loan A aur Loan B do independent loans hain, jinme se har ek ke default hone ki probability 0.8 percent hai aur default loss 1,000 dollars hai. 99 percent confidence par Loan A ka VaR zero hai aur Loan B ka VaR bhi zero hai.

en.display: Merged into a single portfolio, the combined probability of at least one default is 1.59%, causing 99% VaR to surge to $1,000: VaR penalizes diversification!

hi.display: Lekin jab aap dono loans ko ek portfolio mein merge karte hain, toh at least ek loan ke default hone ki probability 1.59 percent ho jaati hai, jo 1 percent se badi hai! Toh combined portfolio ka 99 percent VaR 1,000 dollars ho jata hai! VaR diversification ko penalize karta hai!

scenes.title: Tail Blindness: 'How Bad is Bad?'
scenes.purpose: Tail Blindness: 'How Bad is Bad?': Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Tail Blindness: 'How Bad is Bad?': Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: The second fatal limitation of Value at Risk is Tail Blindness: it marks the 1% boundary but remains completely blind to the severity beyond it.

hi.display: VaR ka dusra fatal flaw hai Tail Blindness. VaR aapko ye batata hai ki 1 percent worst cases kahan se shuru hote hain, lekin us line ke paar loss kitna gehra hai, ye bilkul nahi batata!

en.display: If Portfolio A loses $101 in the tail and Portfolio B suffers a catastrophic $10 million collapse, both report identical 99% VaR cutoffs of $100!

hi.display: Screen par dekhiye: Agar portfolio A tail mein 101 dollars lose karta hai, aur portfolio B tail mein 10 million dollars lose karta hai, dono ka 99 percent VaR exactly identical 100 dollars report hoga!

en.display: Option traders writing deep out-of-the-money puts concealed catastrophic tail risk behind pristine VaR figures until the 2008 financial crisis struck!

hi.display: Deep out-of-the-money options write karne wale traders ne 2008 se pehle isi loophole ka faida uthaya: VaR zero dikhaya aur jab black swan crash aaya toh poora institution liquidate ho gaya!

scenes.title: Expected Shortfall (ES): Coherent Tail Risk
scenes.purpose: Expected Shortfall (ES): Coherent Tail Risk: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Expected Shortfall (ES): Coherent Tail Risk: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: The permanent mathematical solution is Expected Shortfall, also known in quantitative risk literature as Conditional VaR.

hi.display: Is fatal flaw ka permanent mathematical solution hai Expected Shortfall yaani ES, jise Conditional VaR bhi kehte hain.

en.display: Expected Shortfall is formulated as the conditional expectation of loss given that loss exceeds the VaR threshold: the average of all tail losses!

hi.display: Expected Shortfall ka formula hai: E of L given L is greater than VaR. Yaani VaR threshold cross hone ke baad tail ke sabhi catastrophic losses ka conditional average!

en.display: Expected Shortfall is strictly coherent and subadditive under all distributions, leading Basel FRTB to replace 99% VaR with 97.5% Expected Shortfall.

hi.display: Expected Shortfall unconditionally coherent hota hai aur har distribution par Subadditivity satisfy karta hai. Isiliye Basel Committee ne FRTB regulations mein 99 percent VaR ko permanently discard karke 97.5 percent Expected Shortfall mandate kar diya hai!

scenes.title: Historical Simulation: Non-Parametric Engine
scenes.purpose: Historical Simulation: Non-Parametric Engine: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Historical Simulation: Non-Parametric Engine: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: On commercial trading desks, Historical Simulation is the premier risk engine because it imposes zero artificial Gaussian distribution assumptions.

hi.display: Trading desks par VaR aur Expected Shortfall calculate karne ka sabse widely used method hai Historical Simulation. Iska sabse bada edge hai ki ye koi normal distribution ya bell curve assume nahi karta.

en.display: The methodology replays the bank's current portfolio holdings across the actual empirical market moves of the past 500 or 1,000 trading sessions.

hi.display: Hum bank ke current portfolio ko pichle 500 ya 1,000 trading days ke actual market moves par replay karte hain.

en.display: Today's asset values are shocked by historical percentage returns, completely re-pricing all complex non-linear options across every scenario.

hi.display: Formula: Aaj ke asset prices ko historical percentage return se shock kiya jaata hai, aur portfolio ko fully re-price karke 500 hypothetical P&L outcomes generate kiye jaate hain.

scenes.title: Worked Example: 500-Day Historical Simulation
scenes.purpose: Worked Example: 500-Day Historical Simulation: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Worked Example: 500-Day Historical Simulation: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Let us examine concrete numbers for a $20 million portfolio: we rank the 500 simulated scenarios from worst dollar loss to largest gain.

hi.display: Sharma ji, kya hum actual 500-day simulation numbers ke sath dekh sakte hain ki VaR aur Expected Shortfall kaise calculate hote hain?

en.display: At 99% confidence over 500 historical days, the 1% tail threshold corresponds to the 5th worst loss, yielding a 99% VaR of $420,000.

hi.display: Bilkul! Maan lijiye 20 million dollar portfolio hai. Hum 500 dinon ke simulated P&L ko sabse bade loss se profit ki taraf sort karte hain: L 1 se lekar L 500 tak.

en.display: To compute 99% Expected Shortfall, we take the mathematical average of the top 5 worst losses: $750k, $620k, $540k, $480k, and $420k.

hi.display: 99 percent confidence par 500 dinon ka 1 percent hota hai 5th worst loss. Agar 5th worst loss 420,000 dollars hai, toh hamara 99 percent 1-day VaR exactly 420,000 dollars hai!

en.display: The resulting Expected Shortfall is $562,000, successfully impounding the extreme $750,000 tail crash into the bank's capital reserve!

hi.display: Aur 99 percent Expected Shortfall worst 5 losses ka average hota hai: 750k plus 620k plus 540k plus 480k plus 420k divided by 5 equals 562,000 dollars! Dekha Raju? Expected Shortfall ne tail ke catastrophic 750,000 loss ko capture karke true risk reveal kiya!

scenes.title: Interactive Cognitive Quiz
scenes.purpose: Interactive Cognitive Quiz: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Interactive Cognitive Quiz: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: Evaluate the scenario: Portfolio A has a 99% VaR of $100,000 and Portfolio B has a 99% VaR of $150,000. Is combined VaR guaranteed to be less than or equal to $250,000? Consider the options on screen.

hi.display: Raju, ab tumhare liye ek critical institutional risk quiz: Portfolio A ka 99 percent 1-day VaR 100,000 dollars hai, aur Portfolio B ka 99 percent 1-day VaR 150,000 dollars hai. Ek junior risk manager claim karta hai ki combined portfolio A plus B ka VaR maximum 250,000 dollars hi ho sakta hai. Kya ye claim guaranteed true hai?

en.display: Pause and calculate: Recall Artzner's axioms and evaluate whether Value at Risk satisfies subadditivity across non-normal distributions.

hi.display: Is mathematical concept aur financial derivation ko dhyan se samajhiye.

en.display: Option B is correct: Not guaranteed! VaR violates Subadditivity on non-normal distributions, short options, and credit portfolios with heavy jump risk!

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option B: Guaranteed true nahi hai! Kyunki Value at Risk non-normal distributions, short options, aur credit exposures par Subadditivity ko violate kar sakta hai, jisse combined portfolio ka VaR 250,000 dollars se bada ho sakta hai! Sirf Expected Shortfall subadditivity guarantee karta hai!

scenes.title: Volatility Updating in Historical Simulation
scenes.purpose: Volatility Updating in Historical Simulation: Foundational quantitative principles
takeaways: Volatility Updating in Historical Simulation: Foundational quantitative principles

en.display: A standard historical simulation treats a calm market move from two years ago with the exact same weight as yesterday's panic selloff.

hi.display: Standard historical simulation ka ek drawback ye hai ki 2 saal purane calm market data ko kal ke panic shock ke barabar weight milta hai.

en.display: John Hull and Alan White resolved this distortion through Volatility Updating: scaling past percentage returns by the ratio of current volatility to past volatility.

hi.display: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye Hull aur White ne Volatility Updating method invent kiya: historical percentage return ko aaj ki current volatility aur historical volatility ke ratio se scale kiya jaata hai.

en.display: Under market stress, historical scenarios are dynamically magnified to reflect heightened current turbulence, eliminating dangerous risk reporting lag.

hi.display: Isse agar aaj market stressed hai, toh past data current high volatility regime ke hisab se dynamically scale-up ho jata hai, eliminating historical lag!
